entries.description: EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENT: the project's FIRST PROSPECTIVE REPRODUCER, an external reviewer, named a reproduction target -- asked whether the rb-EKF trail (symbolic Jacobian -> normalized form -> certified fixed-point lowering -> emitted RTL -> silicon-capture replay) is reconstructible from PUBLIC artifacts. This is the first time the work has been asked that question by somebody outside it. The orchestrator's direction: walk it ourselves from a clean environment FIRST, and ship a REPRODUCING.md where every step carries a committed expected result.

Set the hostile-stranger conditions rather than letting me choose them: Docker container, fresh user, no host checkouts, no home-directory config, no globally installed packages, no Blackwell toolchains, public remotes only. And the constraint that makes it a real test -- PIN AND RECORD how the repos must sit RELATIVE TO EACH OTHER, because the trail spans multiple repos and a stranger gets no implicit layout. That constraint is what caught the sibling-directory assumption in regenerate_rtl.py.

TWO CLOCKS, NO SHARED DIFFS: nothing this session touches the TT fork, the pinned run-003 RTL, or the chip pre-registration -- the reproduction clock and the tapeout clock must not share a diff. Also scoped OUT the version-echo workflow step for gl_test, licensing it for the additions run and not this one. Both are scope fences set before work started, not after.

DISCLOSED IN THE PRE-REGISTRATION THAT I HAD ALREADY LOOKED. I ran gh repo view on all six candidate repos BEFORE writing the bars, so I knew forge and monogate-research were private when I wrote a divergence class named 'missing public artifact'. Writing a bar around a fact already in hand, without saying so, converts a lookup into a prediction. The prereg therefore states that this class is EXPECTED TO FIRE and that its firing is NOT a successful prediction.

REFUSED TO LET THE ANALYTIC atan THEOREM STAND IN FOR THE ENUMERATION CERTIFICATE. MachLib.Real.eml_atan_full_fwd_error is public and re-derives sorryAx-free in the container, and grading rung iii green on it would have looked entirely convincing. It is the Taylor-remainder result, NOT the exhaustive fixed-point sweep that produces the 6.16e-02 rad worst case. Caught because the bar named the artifact precisely -- 'the atan ENUMERATION certificate' -- and a vaguer bar would have been satisfied by the substitution.

MY OWN COUNT WAS WRONG BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT. I reported 'the published wheel ships 0 tests' from a predicate matching only tests/-prefixed paths; the enumerated figure is 11 test modules, all under tools/machlib_bind/. Conclusion unchanged (none of them is the normalization suite), number wrong. Corrected in the walk log rather than quietly reused -- and caught by re-enumerating, which is luck rather than method.

DID NOT ATTRIBUTE 47 PRE-EXISTING TEST FAILURES TO MY OWN CHANGE. The forge suite showed 47 failures after the emission-gate fix. Rather than assuming they were Lean-related and unrelated, I stashed the change and re-ran the same three files: 11 failed / 31 passed both with and without it. Same discipline as the scope-poisoned-failure-report rule -- attribute the first failure, do not narrate around it.

SPLIT RUNG iii RATHER THAN ROUNDING IT. The bar named two certificates; one re-derives publicly and one does not. Reporting a single grade would have to round in some direction and either direction is false. Recorded as a defect in MY OWN bar sheet -- two questions armed on one bar, discovered by running it, which is the same shape as the chip arc's bars 2 and 3 sharing a run.

OBLIGATION, NOT A JUDGEMENT CALL: push the fixes today. The reasoning given was that the dry run's purpose was to see what a stranger gets, and knowing a stranger gets a broken check_ledger.py and a forge CLI that reports failed emission as success CONVERTS A FOUND DEFECT INTO A KEPT ONE. Also set the sequence: push, publish evidence, wheel + yank + gate, disambiguation, re-walk, then ship.

REFUSED TO LET THE STAGED WALK COUNT. Pointed out that the re-walk had copied fixed files into the container, so the fixed rungs were not demonstrated from PUBLIC state -- and required one more container run, post-push and post-publication, before REPRODUCING.md ships. The document must not assert what only the staged walk demonstrated: its own founding rule applied to itself. This is the intervention that produced every finding after it.

SCOPED THE PUBLICATION DECISION RATHER THAN TAKING IT WHOLE: publish four artifacts, and the fifth (opening the forge repo) does not need deciding this week, because the wheel already makes the compiler publicly installable -- the reproduction needs pip install to work, not read-access to source history. Separating what the reproduction actually requires from what feels like the same question.

NAMED THE STALE WHEEL AS THE arty-tof-raw.v1 CLASS and set the three-part fix: publish from the pinned tree, yank the old version, and gate wheel-vs-tree correspondence in CI. The framing that made it actionable: a version string on a public package index is the strongest identity claim the ecosystem has, and ours was false. Also ruled the machinery moratorium inapplicable because this is a FOUND defect.

DOCUMENTATION, NOT RENAMING, for the ekf_range_bearing name collision -- disambiguate at both ends and do not rename anything pinned. Correctly identified it as the misformalization class E3 was built around: search finds a file, the file is wrong, nothing errors.

GRADUATED STEP 0 FROM INSTRUCTION TO STANDING PROTOCOL, and named what it measured: the deep session's final act -- 'write the two record items and nothing else' -- did not happen, and a fresh head caught it in five minutes. Tail-of-session degradation, measured on TRANSCRIPTION-GRADE work. If that slips at depth, nothing at depth is safe on the strength of being simple.

SHARPENED MY OWN SELF-GRADING INTO A RULE. I had scored the 'at least one breakage' prediction a weak hit; the orchestrator supplied the generalisation -- existence predictions are nearly unfalsifiable against rich outcomes, so predict COUNTS OR CLASSES. Now AMENDMENT 6. I had the observation and stopped at the instance.

Performed the 0.14.0 yank in the PyPI web UI and revoked the exposed API token. Logged as mechanical rather than direction: the decision was already made and the act needed a human at a browser only because PyPI has no yank API -- tokens are upload-scoped and yank sits behind CSRF origin validation. Left 0.14.1 unyanked, which was the judgment call flagged and not made for them.

Yanked 0.14.1 as well, and attached reasons to BOTH releases -- taking the recommended inversion rather than the original plan of reasoning 0.14.1 and leaving 0.14.0 bare. Verified stable on two agreeing reads each.

RULED RE-MEASURE, NOT STAMP, and gave the general rule: a figure inherits the defect history of the instrument that produced it, with three tiers -- re-measure where the defect is known and the re-run is cheap, stamp only where re-measurement is impossible, provenance-by-default going forward. Explicitly REFUSED to authorize a retrospective audit sweep of every historical number (machinery sprawl, moratorium applies). Named the failure mode of my proposal precisely: stamping a stale figure when the instrument that can replace it is already shipped is preserving a caveat instead of doing the measurement.

RULED THE ARMING PROVENANCE RULE: arm bars against the committed artifact, never conversation-transcribed numbers -- and named the distinction precisely as MEMORY-VERSUS-ARTIFACT rather than orchestrator-versus-machine. A bar derived from Action outputs cited by path and hash has artifact provenance regardless of whose hands moved it; a bar from '112,273 as I recall it' is the guessed-threshold defect with extra steps. Also ruled that a missing number is a five-minute transcription commit before arming, not a blocker.

SPECIFIED THE ADDITIONS BAR SHEET: firm on all-corner setup WS, gl_test green including BIST mode, and the CRC expected value derived by a committed script with its hash in the pre-registration -- with the reasoning that a self-test checking a mistyped checksum is the guessed-threshold defect with a NINE-MONTH FEEDBACK LOOP, so the derivation must travel with the bar. MARGINAL on area admissible only with the straddle stated. Theorem-monitor deferred to chip 2 on the record. One scored run if the deltas are attributable apart, CRC-first if not.

findings.description: THE rb-EKF TRAIL IS 2-OF-5 RECONSTRUCTIBLE FROM PUBLIC ARTIFACTS, MEASURED. Walked in a clean container as a fresh user with no host state: the reciprocal certificate and the 57 headline axiom footprints re-derive from public machlib; kernel emission, the normalization soundness suite, the atan enumeration certificate and the silicon-capture replay do not, because the artifacts are private. This falsifies the working assumption the trail was described under -- that a reader could follow it from public sources. Nine findings, by class: missing public artifact 5, environment leakage 2, cross-repo assumption 1, defect-surfaced 1.

THE PUBLISHED WHEEL IS A STALE BUILD UNDER A LIVE VERSION NUMBER. forge the repo is private but forge the compiler is on PyPI, which reopened two rungs I had written off. monogate-forge==0.14.0 ships a verilog_backend.py of 46,741 bytes with ZERO occurrences of ekf2d_filter; the tree at the same declared version has 132,243 bytes and 17. A version string that does not identify an artifact is not a pin. Nobody had ever installed the published package and tried to compile the flagship kernel with it.

A FAILED EMISSION WROTE A COMMENT AND EXITED 0 -- THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE FAMILY IN THIS BACKEND. Seven sites caught CompileError and returned Verilog comment text; compile() returned a str, the CLI wrote a .v, the process exited 0. A GENERATED ARTIFACT THAT REPORTS ITS OWN FAILURE ONLY IN A COMMENT IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM OUTPUT. Same family as assert_normalised_cleanly existing and never being called, and as a missing optional eml_cost silently halving the datapath: all three produced confident output from a mechanism that did not do the job. Fixed with the EXISTING mechanism copied rather than a new one -- accumulator, warn, gate on the shipping path -- specimen asserts the CLI exit code in a subprocess because the precedent is a correct assert that was never invoked.

A PLAUSIBLE WRONG ANSWER SITTING IN A PUBLIC REPO. eml-stdlib publicly ships eml_stdlib/control/ekf_range_bearing.eml. It is NOT the trail's kernel: 60 lines, robot pose (x,y,theta) observing a landmark, sha 5c5d21bf -- against the trail's 28-line 2-D radar tracker sqrt(x0^2+x1^2), atan(x1/x0), sha 31c4eedd. A stranger searching public repos for the source FINDS A FILE AND IT IS THE WRONG ONE. Not an error message, which is what makes it worse than absence.

THE TRAP THE PAGE WARNED ABOUT CAUGHT THE PAGE. The round-1 provenance table declares itself LF-normalised and warns in bold that forge lands CRLF while monogate-research lands LF -- then carries one CRLF row, precisely the one row whose file lives in forge. A reproducer who FOLLOWS THE INSTRUCTION computes 31c4eedd and sees a mismatch against the committed a189f79b. Verified by construction rather than inferred: re-appending CR to the LF form reproduces a189f79b exactly, and the file has a single commit in forge history so content drift is excluded.

UNAVAILABLE MUST ALSO NOT BE A FAIL -- the unstated corollary of house rule 4, found by a clean container. check_ledger.py died with a raw FileNotFoundError traceback and EXIT 1, which is the code it also returns when the axiom trust boundary has genuinely drifted. A reproducer could not tell 'machlib broke' from 'I have not installed elan', and between those a stranger assumes the alarming one. Now exit 2, naming the missing tool, no traceback. The rule was already written as 'UNAVAILABLE is never zero'; nobody had written 'and never a FAIL'.

THE TRAIL IS NOW 5-OF-5 RECONSTRUCTIBLE FROM PUBLIC ARTIFACTS, measured in a container that never saw a host checkout. Emission re-derives to f47f6c81 byte-identically from the published wheel and the published kernel; normalization suite, atan ENUMERATION certificate and silicon-capture replay all run from the public evidence package; the reciprocal certificate and the 57 headline axiom footprints re-derive from public machlib. What closed it was four publications and four defect fixes, not a re-description of what already existed.

47 STANDING TEST FAILURES WERE AN INSTRUMENT DEFECT, AND HAD BEEN EXPLAINED AWAY TWICE IN ONE DAY -- INCLUDING BY ME. They were dismissed as 'pre-existing Lean failures' while checking whether my own change had broken anything, which is the correct check performed and then mis-concluded. Root cause: Lake moved the olean root from .lake/build/lib to .lake/build/lib/lean, discovery still pointed at the parent (which EXISTS and holds no oleans), and lake_available() tested only for the binary while its own docstring admitted the gap. A missing dependency therefore surfaced as a FAILED PROOF. A STANDING RED THAT EVERYONE HAS LEARNED TO EXPLAIN IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM ONE THAT IS TELLING THE TRUTH. Now 1358 passed / 55 skipped / 0 failed -- and that is 47 tests correctly reported as UNMEASURED, not 47 tests fixed.

MY OWN EVIDENCE PACKAGE COMMITTED THE DEFECT CLASS IT WAS PUBLISHED TO FIX, THREE TIMES. (1) The certificate rung shipped without its dependency closure -- and the same commit's message states the rule that prevents it, applied to the neighbouring directory. (2) A vendored copy forked from forge within the hour, so the re-walk debugged a bug that no longer existed anywhere else. (3) The manifest enumerated the working directory and recorded four .pytest_cache files, so it passed for its author and failed for every reader. All three were invisible until the artifact ran in the state a stranger gets. KNOWING THE RULE IS NOT APPLYING IT, and the only thing that closed the gap was execution from outside.

THE WHEEL SHIPPED A C BACKEND WHOSE OUTPUT IT COULD NOT COMPILE. software/runtime/c/libmonogate.h is what the emitted C #includes, and it never entered the wheel: the 'software*' entry in setuptools' find-include discovers PYTHON PACKAGES ONLY, and software/runtime/ had no __init__.py. NOBODY CHOSE THIS -- a discovery rule decided it by omission. Found by pip-installing the wheel and trying to compile what it emitted, which nobody had ever done. My first diagnosis was wrong: I read the config, saw software* in the include list, and concluded the header must ship. Reading the artifact showed zero runtime members. Derive from the artifact, not from what the config says the artifact should be.

THE PUBLICATION PIPELINE WAS THE ONLY LINK IN THE ARTIFACT CHAIN WITH NO GATE, AND 0.14.0 HAD BYPASSED IT ENTIRELY -- the release workflow has no run for that version at all; the last gated release was 0.13.0. So the stale wheel was not a gate failing, it was a gate never invoked. Now gated: the release path builds from a git-archive snapshot of the TAG and diffs the wheel both directions before upload, with exit 2 (could-not-run) deliberately blocking here even though UNAVAILABLE is honestly neither pass nor fail everywhere else -- on a release path, 'we could not check' is not a licence to publish. The gate's first real run caught a real mismatch: my own.

MY OWN VERIFICATION COMMAND READ THE ENDPOINT THAT LIES. After the orchestrator yanked 0.14.0 I checked https://pypi.org/pypi/monogate-forge/json and it reported yanked=False for every release. The yank HAD landed: the PEP 592 simple API and the cache-busted per-version endpoint both report True for the wheel AND the sdist. The aggregate JSON endpoint was serving a stale cached response. Had I stopped there I would have told them their action did not work and sent them back to the browser -- attributing a CDN cache to a human error, which is the scope-poisoned-failure-report family pointed at a person instead of a module. Two independent read paths is what separated them, and the command I had HANDED THEM one message earlier was the wrong one. A verifier is only as good as the endpoint it trusts.

THE PUBLICATION CHAIN IS CLOSED. 0.14.0 -- the stale wheel whose bits did not match its version, published outside the release pipeline that has no CI run for it -- is yanked on PyPI, both wheel and sdist. 0.14.3 is latest, released through the gated path with wheel-vs-tagged-tree correspondence checked before upload. The exposed token is revoked. Residual, recorded rather than closed: the yank carries NO REASON, so a downstream user with 0.14.0 pinned sees a bare warning and cannot judge urgency -- the reason field is what surfaces through installer APIs. And 0.14.1 stays unyanked despite shipping a C backend whose output cannot compile.

MY OWN CORRECTION WAS ALSO WRONG, AND IN THE SAME FAMILY. Earlier today I found the aggregate PyPI JSON serving stale yank state, and concluded: verify on the PEP 592 simple API or the cache-busted per-version endpoint. THAT CONCLUSION IS FALSE. On the next verification the simple API reported 0.14.1 NOT yanked while the per-version JSON showed it yanked with its reason; and a CACHE-BUSTED per-version read reported yanked_reason=None that a second read seconds later had. Every path is eventually consistent and a cache-buster does not defeat it. THE DEFECT IN MY FIX WAS ITS SHAPE: I responded to one stale endpoint by nominating a different endpoint as authoritative, which is the same single-read trust with a new address. The correct rule is procedural, not topological -- RE-READ UNTIL TWO CONSECUTIVE READS AGREE. I came within one command of reporting the orchestrator's completed work as not-done for the SECOND time in one session, from the same root cause, having already written a finding about the first.
findings.artifact_link: monogate experiments/automation/ledger/2026-08-01-repro-dryrun.json — the prior finding it corrects

findings.description: THE SORRY DETECTOR WAS RUBBER-STAMPING SINCE THE v4.32.2 TOOLCHAIN BUMP. Lean changed the quoting of its undischarged-obligation warning from straight quotes to backticks; lean_runner matched the literal old string, so has_sorry was ALWAYS FALSE and full_build_ok reported TRUE FOR PROOFS CONTAINING sorry. A gate that passes everything is indistinguishable from one that is not connected, and this one was not connected. IT WAS NEVER SILENT: five negative-control specimens were failing and saying so in plain English. They sat inside 47 failures that a SEPARATE defect (stale olean discovery) made look environmental, and the block was waved off as pre-existing more than once, including by me while checking whether my own change had broken anything. A CONVICT SPECIMEN THAT FIRES INSIDE A BLOCK OF NOISE HAS NOT FIRED. The cheap defect camouflaged the expensive one; a noisy environmental failure is not merely an annoyance, it is COVER. Disposition of the 47: 42 pass, 5 fail, all five one root cause, now 1422 passed / 1 skipped / 0 failed. Exposure bounded to forge's @verify(lean) close-rate reporting; machlib unaffected (claim_audit keys on sorryAx in a print-axioms footprint, structurally different).

STEP-0 INSTANCE 2: A SCORED RUN'S VERDICT EXISTED ONLY IN CONVERSATION FOR A DAY. Run 003 passed bar 4, demonstrated its convict direction and satisfied the tapeout contingency -- and was never transcribed. The session that produced it also failed to write the bars 2/3 retirement that instance 1 caught, so it failed to write its own HEADLINE. Detected by a summary disagreeing with a memory: a state-of-the-work report described the arc as still waiting on 003, faithfully, because the records said so. The records were wrong. Sharpens the standing protocol from 'audit the previous session's owed amendments' to 'audit its RESULTS' -- an owed amendment is something someone remembered to promise; a result happened whether anyone promised anything or not.

THREE INSTANCES IN ONE DAY MADE A CLASS, AND THE CLASS GOT A TAXONOMY. A missing instrument must never share an exit code with a failed measurement: the axiom ledger gave a missing Lean toolchain the same code as a drifted trust boundary; the Verilog backend gave a failed emission the same code as SUCCESS; the equivalence runner gave a missing dependency the signal of an unproved theorem. Each conflates 'couldn't look' with 'looked and found bad' -- or, in the second case, with 'looked and found good', which is worse. Now project-wide: 0 measured-pass, 1 measured-fail, 2 could-not-measure, and 2 BLOCKS on any path that publishes. Elsewhere UNAVAILABLE is honestly neither pass nor fail; on a shipping path, 'we could not check' is not a licence to publish.
findings.artifact_link: monogate experiments/automation/PROTOCOL.md house rule 4 — the exit-code taxonomy

findings.description: THE REPRODUCTION IS NOW A REGRESSION CHECK RATHER THAN A SNAPSHOT, and it runs on x86-64. Closes the disclosed architecture gap (the reviewer's platform is tested before the reviewer is) and the rot gap, which is the larger one: the job installs the compiler from PyPI so a bad release breaks it, and CLONES FROM THE PUBLIC REMOTE rather than using the workspace, so a file that exists locally but was never committed cannot make the walk pass. That last clause is earned -- three times today an oracle read the working directory instead of the repository, and each version passed for its author and failed for everyone else. actions/checkout would have reproduced exactly that defect in CI. Rung 5 applies the new exit-code taxonomy explicitly: a 2 fails the job, because a reproduction claim cannot rest on a check that did not run.

I FLAGGED A FIGURE AS DEFECT-TAINTED WITHOUT CHECKING WHICH INSTRUMENT PRODUCED IT. I called the @verify(lean) close rate unquotable because it was 'produced by the detector that was rubber-stamping'. It was not: closerate.sh is machlib-side and matches the pattern 'uses .sorry.' with WILDCARDS, so it matched both quotings and never went blind. Applied properly, the inherits-the-defect-history rule EXONERATES that figure -- I applied it by association, which is the same shortcut as blaming the nearest recent change. A rule used only to convict is not being used, it is being invoked. SECOND NEAR-MISS IN THE SAME SWEEP: against the 93.6% I had in mind, the measured 77.1% reads as a 16.5-point collapse and my pre-registered disconfirmer fired -- but 93.6% is 264/282 mach_linarith SUBSTANTIVE closes, a different corpus. The comparable documented figure is 76%, so 77.1% is marginally ABOVE it on a corpus 4.3x larger. Two confident precise wrong stories avoided in one measurement, both by checking a definition before quoting a delta.

THE @verify(lean) CLOSE RATE IS QUOTABLE AGAIN, WITH PROVENANCE AND BOTH DENOMINATORS: 77.1% (553/717) of assessable obligations, or 73.8% (553/749) including 4 stale files that do not compile, measured by closerate.sh at machlib HEAD under Lean v4.32.2. Both denominators ship together because excluding the stale files FLATTERS the number, and 'of everything the corpus claims' is what an outsider means. Residual named rather than dropped: mul_mat4, vec3, autopilot, shadow_pcf -- 32 theorems, 4.3% of the corpus, do not build at all.

THE RUN-LEVEL CONCLUSION FOR RUN 003 IS 'failure' AND NO BAR FAILED. gds, precheck and gl_test all succeeded; the VIEWER job -- GDS rendering for the docs site, no bar attached -- is the only failure, and it alone colours the run red. A reader checking 'did 003 pass?' via gh run list gets the OPPOSITE of the truth. Same defect as a green job hiding steps that never ran, opposite sign -- and the RED direction is the one nobody double-checks, because a false red gets believed and abandoned while a false green at least gets used until it breaks. Almost certainly why the arc's headline result sat untranscribed for a day: the run reads as a failure at a glance.

A REMEMBERED NUMBER WAS WRONG ON EXACTLY THE FIGURE A BAR WAS ABOUT TO LEAN ON. Of three run-003 figures carried in conversation, two survived contact with the artifacts perfectly (area 112,273 um² exact; worst slack +0.665 vs measured +0.6648566) and one did not: utilisation headroom carried as ~29%, measured 24.74%. The additions run intended to arm a MARGINAL area straddle against that headroom -- a bar built on 17% more room than the die has. THE FAILURE IS NOT CARELESSNESS, IT IS SILENCE: two of three carried perfectly, so nothing signalled which one to distrust, and the wrong one landed on the load-bearing quantity. This is the guessed-threshold defect arriving as a REMEMBERED number rather than an invented one, which is harder to catch because it feels like a measurement. Direct vindication of the arm-from-artifacts rule, on its first application.

EXTERNAL REVIEW: 8/10, AND EVERY DEDUCTION MATCHED A LIMITATION WE HAD ALREADY PUBLISHED. The same reviewer who three exchanges earlier called the loop "closer to a roadmap than a solved problem" moved to 8/10, with the delta explained entirely by artifacts they could check rather than arguments they were offered. The composition matters more than the magnitude: curated-not-arbitrary is the concession from our first reply; artifact-verification-not-re-measurement is REPRODUCING.md's own rung grading; single-board/single-designer/zero-reproductions is Row 9 of the accountability page; private-source-public-wheel is the disclosed posture. Their "why not higher" section is our own graded-claims inventory read back to us, with independent agreement on the grades.

ZERO PREVIOUSLY-UNKNOWN GAPS. That is the headline. An adversarial-adjacent reader, armed with the artifacts and with no reason to be kind, found nothing we had not already named. It is the strongest available evidence that the self-grading is calibrated -- self-assessment is normally unfalsifiable, and this is the one experiment that can falsify it: a stranger arriving at the same map of what is proven and what is not.

PROVENANCE, STATED: the score and its reasoning are orchestrator-relayed and exist only in conversation. No issue was filed on the public repo, no artifact was fetched, and nothing in any repository records the reviewer's identity, the date, or the channel. This entry is a transcription, the same class as run 003's verdict before it was re-derived -- and unlike that one there is no artifact to go and fetch.
findings.artifact_link: conversation, orchestrator-relayed — no artifact exists; see the provenance clause in the entry

findings.description:
DERIVED QUANTITIES ARE THE ONES MEMORY INVENTS -- the mechanism behind the headroom catch, not just the catch. Of three run-003 figures carried in conversation, the two that survived contact with the artifacts perfectly were EXACT-LOOKING and distinctive (112,273 um²; +0.665 ns), and the one that was wrong was DERIVED (~29% headroom, actually 24.74%). That is a selection effect, not bad luck: distinctive numbers get carried verbatim because there is nothing to do but copy them, while derived quantities get carried as impressions, because somebody once did the division and the result felt round. So remembered figures fail precisely where derivation entered -- and derivation enters exactly at the quantities bars get built on, because a bar is almost always a comparison against something computed rather than something read.

TWO CONSEQUENCES. First, "arm from artifacts" cannot be a spot-check discipline: nothing about the two exact matches signalled that the third was rotten, so the property is all-or-nothing per bar sheet. Second, the failure has a long fuse -- a MARGINAL area bar armed on 17% phantom headroom would have been discovered only when a passing addition mysteriously failed placement, which is the guessed-threshold defect with a ten-day delay instead of an immediate contradiction. Caught at cost zero because the rule was applied to every figure rather than the suspicious one.

THE REVIEW-TO-GRADE CORRESPONDENCE CHECK, established today as a repeatable reading discipline. Any external review can be scored the same way: cross-reference each deduction against the published limitations, and treat UNMATCHED DEDUCTIONS as the alarm -- a gap someone found that we had not named. Today that count is zero, which is the baseline. The paper's eventual referees will produce the same kind of list, and there is now both a method for reading it and a number to read it against.

Costs nothing to run and turns every review into a calibration event rather than a verdict to absorb. It is also the only instrument in this program that can falsify the self-grading from outside: an internal audit of our own claims can always be generous in a way we cannot see, whereas an unmatched deduction is a stranger pointing at a hole we did not know we had.
